topic-024-488-solutions-to-the-xor-probl.evolution: The collection begins with foundational network classifiers and decision systems in 1987. Work through the 1990s studies internal-representation search, node splitting, weight decay, and overfitting in simple models. Recent representatives explore connectivity between trained solutions, alternative credit assignment, and forward-growing polynomial forecasters; these are related questions, not evidence of one uninterrupted research lineage.
openQuestions: Which constructive architectures retain competitive performance while exposing useful structure?
How can simple learning models reveal failures that persist at modern scale?
topic-024-488-solutions-to-the-xor-probl.overview: This historically broad cluster asks how neural networks acquire internal representations, how their architecture should grow, and why training can overfit. Early examples examine perceptrons, hidden-unit construction, alternative learning objectives, and regularization. Later papers revisit model symmetries and local learning mechanisms, with some constructive architectures offering interpretable alternatives to end-to-end backpropagation.
topic-024-488-solutions-to-the-xor-probl.title: Neural Learning Dynamics and Constructive Architectures
topic-024-488-solutions-to-the-xor-probl.whyItMatters: Representing a function is different from learning it reliably from finite data. Architecture, training dynamics, and stopping rules interact, so even a realizable task can produce poor generalization.

topic-025-de-randomized-smoothing-for-de.evolution: Early papers examine accurate, diverse members and bagging-like methods. Later work studies hyperparameter ensembles and uncertainty-aware selection. Recent analyses expose collusion under joint training and qualify robustness claims, while adaptive stacking-and-cascading methods seek ensemble quality without evaluating every member for every input.
openQuestions: How can training encourage diversity that remains useful out of distribution?
When is another ensemble prediction more valuable than allocating compute to one stronger model?
topic-025-de-randomized-smoothing-for-de.overview: Ensembles combine predictors to improve decisions, but their benefits depend on the quality and genuine complementarity of members. This topic studies diversity, uncertainty, distribution shift, and efficient execution. Representative work questions whether apparent disagreement generalizes and whether a larger single model can reproduce benefits attributed to ensembling.
topic-025-de-randomized-smoothing-for-de.title: Ensemble Diversity, Calibration, and Adaptive Inference
topic-025-de-randomized-smoothing-for-de.whyItMatters: Training several models costs more, and diversity metrics can reward differences that do not help on new data. Useful ensembles need evaluation against equally capable alternatives and procedures that spend additional computation only when it improves the decision.

topic-026-k-2-vae-a-koopman-kalman-enhan.evolution: The earliest representatives use recurrent models, direct multi-step prediction, and mixtures of experts. Recent work adds spectral attention and multi-domain pretraining. The 2025–2026 examples use continuous generative objectives, adaptive transfer, multiscale tokenization, and unified masking to extend beyond point forecasting toward probabilistic prediction, reconstruction, and broader time-series analysis.
openQuestions: What makes a pretraining corpus representative of unseen temporal regimes?
How can probabilistic forecasts remain calibrated when resolution or domain changes?
topic-026-k-2-vae-a-koopman-kalman-enhan.overview: Time-series models must capture temporal structure across different variables, sampling patterns, and application domains. This cluster includes recurrent forecasting, spectral representations, probabilistic prediction, and large pretrained models. The recent focus is on reusable representations that support new datasets or tasks without extensive retraining.
topic-026-k-2-vae-a-koopman-kalman-enhan.title: General Time-Series Forecasting and Foundation Models
topic-026-k-2-vae-a-koopman-kalman-enhan.whyItMatters: A model tuned to one dataset may fail when its frequency content, horizon, or uncertainty changes. General forecasting requires both shared structure and mechanisms that preserve domain-specific information rather than assuming all temporal data behave alike.

topic-027-4dgcpro-efficient-hierarchical.evolution: Earlier representatives address video time-series and rendering, followed by hierarchical future prediction. Recent work emphasizes one-step diffusion, dynamic token reduction, and history-guided generation. The 2026 examples combine persistent context, importance-aware cache compression, and memory-aware distillation to support longer videos and interactive control.
openQuestions: Which past frames must remain accessible to preserve geometry after revisiting a scene?
Can speedup methods retain rare but important motion details over long rollouts?
topic-027-4dgcpro-efficient-hierarchical.overview: Video generation must maintain motion, identity, and scene geometry while controlling the cost of processing many frames. These papers study diffusion acceleration, history conditioning, frame interpolation, super-resolution, and streaming world models. Memory design is central because earlier frames can contain information needed to prevent long-horizon drift.
topic-027-4dgcpro-efficient-hierarchical.title: Efficient and Temporally Consistent Video Generation
topic-027-4dgcpro-efficient-hierarchical.whyItMatters: High-quality short clips do not establish that a model can sustain a coherent interactive scene. Practical systems need efficient inference and selective retention of context without accumulating visual errors or losing important spatial relationships.

topic-028-textit-neuropath-a-neural-path.evolution: Early representatives investigate predictive sequence learning and functional localization. Later work builds local learning rules for recurrent spiking networks and reverse-engineers task solutions. Recent studies connect feedback control to credit assignment while demonstrating mechanistic mismatches under partial observation, and explore structural-to-functional communication models across regions.
openQuestions: What interventions distinguish competing circuit models that fit the same recordings?
Which local learning mechanisms support both rapid correction and durable adaptation?
topic-028-textit-neuropath-a-neural-path.overview: Computational neuroscience uses recurrent networks to explain how neural activity supports behavior and learning. This cluster examines local plasticity, feedback control, long-term dependencies, and communication between brain regions. It also tests whether a model that reproduces recorded activity truly recovers the underlying mechanism.
topic-028-textit-neuropath-a-neural-path.title: Neural Circuit Dynamics and Biological Credit Assignment
topic-028-textit-neuropath-a-neural-path.whyItMatters: Matching observed trajectories can hide incorrect internal dynamics, especially when recordings sample only a small fraction of a circuit. Mechanistic explanations need validation beyond prediction accuracy and learning rules compatible with biological constraints.

topic-029-delta-mathrm-energy-optimizing.evolution: Earlier papers examine language modulation and visual-question-answering biases. Later work improves alignment with frozen language models. Recent examples quantify visual information gain, study retrieval-induced distraction, and distill region-level supervision into single-pass perception, aiming to make visual reliance stronger without expensive inference-time tool use.
openQuestions: Can visual contribution be measured without rewarding sensitivity to irrelevant pixels?
How can region-focused supervision improve detail recognition without weakening global understanding?
topic-029-delta-mathrm-energy-optimizing.overview: Vision-language systems must align visual representations with language while ensuring that images contribute to the answer. This topic studies language priors, selective training, efficient multimodal computation, and fine-grained perception. The representatives ask both how to connect pretrained components and how to identify examples or tokens whose predictions genuinely depend on visual evidence.
topic-029-delta-mathrm-energy-optimizing.title: Visual Evidence Use in Vision-Language Models
topic-029-delta-mathrm-energy-optimizing.whyItMatters: A model can answer familiar questions from linguistic shortcuts while missing small but decisive image details. Training and evaluation should distinguish visual contribution from fluent guessing and account for the cost of repeated inspection.

topic-030-a-consistent-regularization-ap.evolution: The collection spans early learning from structured objects and max-margin models. The 2000s representatives examine compatible approximate inference and dual losses. More recent work studies certified generalization and learnable dynamic-program parameters, including efficient second-order derivatives needed to train alignment and parsing marginals end to end.
openQuestions: Which relaxations preserve the predictions that matter after discretization?
How can learned inference parameters retain meaningful constraints outside the training distribution?
topic-030-a-consistent-regularization-ap.overview: Structured prediction learns outputs such as alignments, matchings, or parse trees whose components must satisfy joint constraints. These papers connect parameter learning with the optimization used to decode a valid structure. Large-margin objectives, convex relaxations, and differentiable dynamic programs offer different ways to make inference part of training.
topic-030-a-consistent-regularization-ap.title: Structured Prediction and Differentiable Inference
topic-030-a-consistent-regularization-ap.whyItMatters: An accurate approximation to an inference score can still mislead a learning algorithm or make good predictions unreachable. Guarantees must therefore cover the combination of training objective and inference procedure, not only each component in isolation.

topic-031-a-consistent-and-efficient-eva.evolution: Earlier representatives study watermark attacks and neural steganography. Recent generative-model work adds latent and model-integrated marks alongside removal and copying studies. The 2026 evaluation examples distinguish artifact-based and semantic watermark properties, seeking more interpretable assessments across generators and watermark families.
openQuestions: How can provenance systems jointly resist erasure and false attribution?
Which benchmarks capture adaptive attacks without confusing visual quality with security?
topic-031-a-consistent-and-efficient-eva.overview: Image watermarks aim to support attribution or provenance by embedding detectable signals, while related methods protect styles or hide information. This cluster examines both construction and failure: removal, forgery, transfer, and evaluation of residual or semantic marks. Robustness includes preventing false attribution, not merely retaining a signal after ordinary image edits.
topic-031-a-consistent-and-efficient-eva.title: Image Watermarking, Provenance, and Adversarial Evaluation
topic-031-a-consistent-and-efficient-eva.whyItMatters: A detector’s positive result is useful only if the mark is difficult to forge and its interpretation is clear. Security evaluations must consider both missing genuine marks and falsely assigning an unrelated image to a source.
